description: Typed, schema-driven traceability for safety-critical software: YAML artifacts, validation, coverage, release gating and compliance evidence. Rust CLI, MCP server, VS Code.
rules: The full reference is in docs/reference, one file per topic; `rivet docs <topic>` prints the same text offline and `rivet docs --list` lists the topics.

Artifacts are YAML files under the paths listed in `sources:` of rivet.yaml. Create and change them with `rivet add` and `rivet modify` rather than by hand, then run `rivet validate`, which exits non-zero on errors.
Filters are s-expressions whose head is an operator, never a field name: `rivet list --filter '(= type "requirement")'`.
Only `rivet verify <ID>` sets an artifact's status to verified, and it refuses without a `verifies` link or a `// rivet: verifies <ID>` source marker.
A release is the set of artifacts with a `release:` field; `rivet release status <version>` exits non-zero until every one is release-ready.
